summary: The FOMC decision lands Tuesday, with new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh holding rates at 3.50–3.75% — but fed funds futures now price a hike, not a cut, as the more likely year-end move. Markets are bracing for Warsh's tone and whether he scraps the dot plot. April CPI already printed at 3.8% year-over-year — the highest since May 2023 — keeping real rates elevated and weighing on gold and crypto.
tweet: Warsh's first FOMC presser as Fed chair lands Wednesday — a hold is priced in, but traders will parse every word for signals on hikes vs. cuts.
